claims.claim: Release date and author: blog 'Introducing System One Models & Jev' is dated Sep 15, 2026, byline Diogo Almeida, founder, TypeSafe, at the URL typesafe.ai/blog/introducing-system-one-models-and-jev.
claims.values: 2026-09-15; Diogo Almeida

claims.checks_gpt: R2: 2026-09-15 at that URL (correct). R1: '2026-01' and 'Diogo Almeida' (date wrong, author correct); R1 elsewhere '2026年9月' (correct)

claims.claim: Definition: a System One model is a class of frontier models built to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly; Jev is 'a frontier-intelligence function call: unstructured state in, typed probabilistic decisions out.'
claims.quote: a new class of frontier models built to make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly
claims.limits: Marketing definition.

claims.claim: Docs definition: System One model makes fast, structured decisions that software can use directly; it evaluates a state and returns typed answers and probabilities, not generated text. Terms: typed decisions (answers limited to a defined set), state, primitives, calibration, confidence, System 1 / System 2 after Kahneman.
claims.quote: make fast, structured decisions that software can use directly
claims.values: State: text only (strings, JSON objects, arrays of text); images/audio/video not supported at time of that page
claims.limits: WebFetch paraphrase; the 'images not yet supported' line predates jev-1.14.0 danger-zone images (A-15).

claims.claim: Training method: Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD), contrasted with RLHF and RLVR. Optimizes 'calibrated decisions: answers with epistemically honest probabilities on System One tasks'. New architecture, parallel sampler, new training method are announced but not described.
claims.quote: training method we call Reinforcement Learning for Calibrated Decisions (RLCD)
claims.limits: No paper; architecture not disclosed (primer A-11 discloses none).

claims.claim: TypeSafe's own pages do not say the training data is synthetic. Synthetic-only training is reported from an Almeida interview.
claims.limits: Interview claim as reported by TechCrunch; the launch-post FAQ 'Where does our training data come from?' exists but its answer was collapsed/not visible to me. Primer (A-11) does not mention synthetic data.

claims.claim: Architecture undisclosed. Press says 'transformer-based, not an LLM'; outside observers suspect an open-weight LLM base; third parties repeat that parameter count/training compute are unpublished. 'Pointer-head' is not a TypeSafe term; the pointer head belongs to Kev, a third-party open reproduction by Jared Palmer, per OrcaRouter.
claims.quote: Almeida is tight-lipped about the model's architecture
claims.limits: Pointer-head attribution to Kev comes from OrcaRouter (A-26/vendor blog snippet 'jev-vs-kev'), not from the Kev repo text I saw (A-31 mentions LoRA + head only through OrcaRouter).

claims.claim: TypeSafe does not state a parameter count. I found no '4.69B' in any TypeSafe page or in the OrcaRouter pages I read (OrcaRouter says size, architecture and training compute are undisclosed).
claims.locator: jev-vs-laya, 'Jev is the closed counterpart' paragraph
claims.values: no size published
claims.limits: I cannot prove a negative across all OrcaRouter posts; searched Exa for '4.69B' + Jev and got no hit.
claims.checks_gpt: CHAT: Jev '4.69B' parameters (from an OrcaRouter blog)

claims.claim: Question primitives: noul (yes/no, returns probability of yes in 0-1, no confidence field), choice (one of up to 255 options; returns choice, probabilities, confidence), score (ordered levels, 2-10; returns score, legend, probabilities, confidence). Version 1.14.0 adds a 'box' type (bounding box) behind a danger-zone header.
claims.locator: OpenAPI examples + Question oneOf; primitive pages A-06
claims.values: noul: 0.98 example; score example 1.7 with legend keys '0','1','2'; box fields top/bottom/left/right
claims.checks_gpt: R1/R2/CHAT: noul/choice/score; outputs probabilities and confidence; no free text

claims.claim: Exact request fields: top level model, state (string|object|array), questions (map id -> question, minProperties 1), optional assets. Each question: type, instructions, criteria (choice: map option->description; score: ordered array; noul: optional {true,false}). Question ids are not sent to the model.
claims.values: model, state, questions, assets; type, instructions, criteria
claims.checks_gpt: CHAT: field names state, questions, type, instructions, criteria

claims.claim: Exact response fields: model (versioned id that answered), answers (map keyed by question id; each has type plus noul | choice+confidence+probabilities | score+confidence+legend+probabilities | box), usage {input_tokens, output_tokens}.
claims.values: example model 'jev-1.13.0' in quickstart raw response

claims.claim: Any number of questions per call: no limit on question count, only the context limits (64k per request, 32k per question; 262k with long-context header). Adding questions 'barely changes the response time'; cookbook says 13 questions in one call is 11.5x cheaper and 9.6x faster than 13 separate calls.
claims.quote: There is no limit on the number of questions in a request.
claims.locator: How many questions you can ask / Ask multiple questions together
claims.values: 11.5x cheaper, 9.6x faster for 13 questions (self-reported cookbook)
claims.limits: Third-party sysone-bench measured 925-1068 ms for a five-question call (A-28), so latency does grow with state size.
claims.checks_gpt: CHAT: any number of questions per call with only slightly more latency

claims.claim: Headline speed/cost claims: homepage '193.6x Faster, 444.6x Cheaper' (workflow evals, 'on the higher end of real world gains'); launch post '40x-200x faster' for System One shaped queries; end-to-end 70ms-500ms vs 3-329 s for frontier LLMs.
claims.quote: we expect that these are on the higher end of real world gains
claims.values: 193.6x faster, 444.6x cheaper; 40x-200x faster; 70-500 ms; Jev $0.000081 vs LLMs $0.013880; 0.114 s vs 8.566 s (homepage example)
claims.limits: Four TypeSafe-built workflows; reference labels = average of GPT-6 Astra and Claude Fable 5.1; LLM baselines run through TypeSafe's own wrapper; latency measured from laptops on the West Coast.
claims.checks_gpt: R2: '100~200x faster' than LLMs. R1: '几十倍快、成本低百倍'

claims.claim: Price: $0.042 per million input tokens = $42 per BILLION input tokens; output tokens free.
claims.quote: Input tokens: $0.042 / MTok ($ 42 per billion tokens). Output tokens: FREE
claims.locator: Frontiers table, Cost row; docs Models page (A-10): '$42 / $0.042' per Btok / Mtok
claims.values: $0.042 per Mtok
claims.limits: TypeSafe says it cannot prove the price is unsubsidized.
claims.checks_gpt: R2: '$42 per million input tokens, output free'

claims.claim: Latency figures 236-276 ms are third-party p50 measurements (AbdelStark/jev-benchmarks 236-256 ms; nibzard DMB 264-276 ms), quoted via Laya and OrcaRouter. TypeSafe states 70-500 ms end to end; the docs say 'most queries complete in about 100 ms' and list no latency SLA.
claims.quote: Most queries complete in about 100 ms.
claims.locator: How to build with TypeSafe - Fast
claims.values: 236-276 ms p50 (third party); 70-500 ms (TypeSafe)
claims.limits: Third-party p50s include network from the tester's location; sourced second-hand through competitor Laya (A-27) and OrcaRouter (A-26).

claims.claim: Model versions: jev-1.13.0 (launch Sep 15, 2026) and jev-1.14.0 (available from Oct 14, 2026). Aliases: jev-latest -> jev-1.13.0 (stable, SDK default), jev-preview -> jev-1.14.0. Blog says jev-latest will move to 1.14.0 a week after Oct 14; 60-day (1.13.0) and 30-day (1.14.0) deprecation notice planned, policy to be published. Response model field returns the versioned id.
claims.values: jev-1.13.0, jev-1.14.0, jev-latest, jev-preview
claims.limits: Docs snapshot still pointed jev-latest at 1.13.0 when I read it (Oct 23); blog says 1.14.0 later. A-15 only read via WebFetch summary.

claims.claim: Wikipedia article 'Jev (AI model)' exists: developer TypeSafe AI, release 15 Sept 2026, stable release jev-1.13.0, license Proprietary; says founded 2024 by Almeida, Gafni, Sheng; claims limited early access with 'US$40 million seed round led by DCVC'; says trained exclusively on synthetic data via RLCD; architecture unpublished; '40-200x faster and 40-400x cheaper'.
claims.locator: infobox and sections Background, Technical specification, Training, Performance
claims.limits: Secondary. 'US$40 million seed' conflicts with TypeSafe's own Series A post ($870M at $7.5B, Oct 9) only in time (seed vs later round); Forbes headline in its reference list says '$200 Million Startup'. '40-400x cheaper' is not in TypeSafe's launch post (post gives 444.6x on homepage and price comparison) - the 40-400x appears in a founder thread per other sources (A-28 snippets). The 'suspected Brier-score loss' line is editorial speculation by Wikipedia.

claims.claim: TypeSafe's own benchmark is 'Workflow evals' at evals.typesafe.ai: four workflows (security incidents, agent-trace observability, invoice processing, customer service), accuracy measured against consensus labels from GPT-6 Astra + Claude Fable 5.1 at high thinking; every model in workflow vs prompt mode. TypeSafe publicly states it will not publish a standard benchmark table.
claims.quote: no standard benchmark table in our model releases
claims.values: per third-party transcription: Jev 67.8% accuracy, $0.0004/case, 0.4 s (read 2026-09-24)
claims.limits: Per-workflow numbers read through systemonemodels.org (A-28), not first-hand; I read only snippets of A-19.

claims.claim: 'Decision Index', 'decision-v7' and 'JevBench' are NOT TypeSafe publications. Jev Decision Index: community HF Space (multimodalart) and repo apolinario/decision-index ('Not affiliated with TypeSafe AI'; 37 public benchmarks, five areas; Full score = private tests; edition 0.4 live). Artificial Analysis also launched a separate Decision Index on 2026-10-13 (per A-28, not verified). decision-v7 is the training/eval suite of Jared Palmer's Kev (10 public datasets + generated policy/rule examples). JevBench: several unrelated projects (Benchmark Heaven v1.6.1; fstandhartinger; dhruvmehra; jevbench.xyz), all independent.
claims.locator: README intro; A-31 Training; A-29 header
claims.values: Jev on Jev Decision Index: Full 60.11, third of 117 rows (data file 2026-10-10, edition 0.3.1, per A-28); on Benchmark Heaven JevBench v0.3.0 page: Capability 77.1 for Jev 1.13.0
claims.limits: None of these is peer reviewed; editions/scales are not comparable across boards; I read only highlights.

claims.claim: Official calibration/threshold guidance: confidence in [0,1] derived from probabilities; low confidence means do not act (escalate, ask, fall back). Example thresholds: <0.5 route to human; destructive actions auto only above 0.9; banking example <0.6 to human, transfer auto >0.85, 0.6-0.85 confirm. Thresholds are domain-dependent; test with your own data. Docs do not discuss calibration metrics beyond the definition.
claims.values: choice: (pmax-1/n)/(1-1/n); noul: no confidence field, use |2p-1|; score: max(0, 1 - sum p_i|i-m| / MAD_unif)
claims.limits: Third-party tests (A-28/A-27 digests) report weak calibration on some datasets (ECE 0.063-0.281; DMB ECE 0.246) - not verified first-hand.

claims.claim: Official use cases: classification, routing, scoring, extraction, branching; map-reduce over big data; real-time; verification/guardrails (jailbreak detection, citation check); model routing; RAG passage classification and reranking; moderation; semantic lint; feature extraction. Docs also list known weaknesses of jev-1.13: literal reading, counting, math/dates, option order bias (leans to first option), adversarial text in state, not for generation.

Enterprise: SOC 2 Type II report on request via Trust Center; zero data retention for enterprise customers (ask sales); no training on customer inputs/outputs; higher rate limits via sales (sales@typesafe.ai). Rate limits are per organization (tokens/s and requests/s), actual numbers only in the console; 429 on exceed; 529 overloaded.
claims.quote: We don’t use your prompts or other inputs to train or fine-tune models.
claims.locator: Your Data / FAQ; A-10 Rate limits
claims.values: body limit 32 MiB (A-12)
claims.limits: Cloudflare's listing also shows 'Zero data retention: Yes' for typesafe/jev (A-33). I saw no BAA, region, or VPC answers.

claims.claim: Fine-tuning on customer data is not offered: the models page says Jev is not fine-tuned or LoRA-adapted with customer data; same weights for all accounts; customization via state/instructions/criteria and by training your own downstream model on Jev's probabilities.
claims.quote: the same weights serve every account

claims.claim: Private deployment / VPC / on-prem: no official offering found. Enterprise FAQ lists the question 'Can we run Jev in our own VPC or on-premises?' but the extracted text shows no answer; docs describe hosted access only; third-party sites say no self-hosting. Distribution partners: Vercel AI Gateway (typesafe-ai/jev), Cloudflare Workers AI (typesafe/jev), OpenRouter, OrcaRouter; Amazon Bedrock not listed (per jev-ai.pro).
claims.limits: FAQ answer may be hidden in a collapsed accordion; not verified in a rendered browser. Partner list is from third-party pages (A-32, A-33, plus snippets).

claims.claim: Terms TypeSafe uses: 'System One model' (class; docs 'System One' / 'System 1' only in the Kahneman explanation), 'typed decisions' / 'typed, probabilistic decisions', 'calibrated decisions', 'state', 'primitives' (questions: Choice, Score, Noul, Box), 'machine-native intelligence', 'smart if-statements', 'frontier-intelligence function call'. The name Jev honors William Stanley Jevons; System One honors Kahneman's System 1.
claims.quote: Think of Jev as a frontier-intelligence function call

claims.claim: Context and input: 64k tokens per request, 32k per question; opt-in long context 262k via header TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Long-Context: true (slower, less accurate, same per-token price). Choice max 255 options. Input is text; images only via TypeSafe-Danger-Zone-Images: true (1.14). English primary language; CJK handled less well.
claims.values: 64k / 32k / 262k tokens; 255 options
claims.limits: InfoQ's '32,000-token context window' is only the per-question figure.

claims.claim: Funding/company facts on TypeSafe's own site: Series A led by Andreessen Horowitz with Sequoia and DCVC, $870 million at a $7.5B valuation, announced Oct 9, 2026; claims 'a third of the Fortune 500' using Jev.
claims.limits: The Fortune 500 line is a company claim; TechCrunch repeats it as 'the startup claims'.

claims.claim: Customer case study (self-published): Jack & Jill replaced Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite for one candidate-scoring stage; reported 88% lower cost, median time 20.3 s -> 10.3 s, winners kept 93.9% -> 94.6% (difference not significant), AUC 0.924 -> 0.933; tested on 150 live roles.
claims.values: $0.755 vs $0.092 per 1,000 candidates; $500K projected annual saving
claims.limits: Customer-run offline test; $500K is a projection.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R2: '$42 per million input tokens, output free'
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Wrong by 1000x. TypeSafe prices Jev at $42 per BILLION input tokens = $0.042 per million; output free.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: R1: blog 'Introducing System One Models & Jev' dated 2026-01
gpt_discrepancies.finding: Page is dated Sep 15, 2026 (byline Diogo Almeida). R1's 'Diogo Almeida' and 'September 2026' elsewhere are right; the January date is wrong. R2's date and URL are correct.

TypeSafe's blog says 40x-200x faster (comparable intelligence, System One-shaped queries); homepage says 193.6x faster and 444.6x cheaper on its own four workflow evals and itself calls these 'the higher end of real world gains'. Independent runs found roughly 5x-25x (see systemonemodels.org digest, secondary).

TypeSafe has not disclosed architecture; 'pointer head' is a feature of the third-party open reproduction Kev (per OrcaRouter), not of Jev. Press only says transformer-based and, per observers, perhaps built on an open-weight LLM.

gpt_discrepancies.gpt: CHAT: Jev '4.69B' parameters (from an OrcaRouter blog)
gpt_discrepancies.finding: No TypeSafe statement of size; OrcaRouter pages I read say parameter count is undisclosed. '4.69B' not found.

These are third-party p50s (AbdelStark pilot, nibzard DMB), reported second-hand by Laya/OrcaRouter, not TypeSafe's figure. TypeSafe's published range is 70-500 ms end to end; docs say about 100 ms for most queries.

None is a TypeSafe benchmark. TypeSafe's own is Workflow evals (evals.typesafe.ai) and it publicly refuses a standard benchmark table. decision-v7 is Kev's training/eval suite; Decision Index and JevBench are independent community or third-party projects (several different 'JevBench's).
